title: Energy Transfer Celebrates 125 Years of the Nederland Terminal
summary: On November 4, 2026, Energy Transfer celebrated the 125th anniversary of the Nederland Terminal with an event featuring employees, retirees, business partners, community leaders and local dignitaries.
body_markdown:
*The largest singularly owned above-ground crude oil storage facility in the U.S. and the largest NGL export facility in the world.*


The year was 1901. Theodore Roosevelt was sworn in as president following the assassination of William McKinley. The Wright brothers’ first powered flight and the first World Series were still two years away. In Southeast Texas, an oil discovery at Spindletop launched the Texas oil boom. Later that year, 42 acres along the Neches River were purchased by the Pew brothers, founders of Sun Oil Company (later Sunoco), for what would become the Nederland Terminal.


One hundred and twenty-five years later, it’s still in operation and serves as a global gateway for crude oil, refined products and natural gas liquids. On November 4, 2026, Energy Transfer celebrated that 125-year milestone with an event at the terminal featuring employees, retirees, business partners, community leaders and local dignitaries.


Energy Transfer co-CEOs Tom Long and Mackie McCrea addressed the crowd and presented Vice President of Nederland Operations Greg Mesthos with a commemorative plaque. They also presented a time capsule to be opened 125 years from now, on November 4, 2151. Among the items placed in the time capsule were that day’s edition of the *Beaumont Enterprise* newspaper, a vial of oil from the terminal, a commemorative coin and an iPhone.


In their remarks, Long and McCrea thanked current and former employees for their service and reflected on the people behind the terminal’s success.


“This is clearly a critical asset not just within Energy Transfer, but it’s a critical asset for our entire country and the energy independence we’ve achieved,” said Long. “We are going to continue building on the legacy that has been left behind and for all the employees here, thank you for what you all are accomplishing every day. It is absolutely fabulous.”


“This facility is the epitome of Energy Transfer,” said McCrea. “When everything is going fine, it’s working well and everything is great. But when things get tough and we get 30 inches of rain, people camp out and we do everything we can to keep volumes flowing, and that’s so beneficial to our partnership, to upstream producers and downstream markets. The work ethic and what you do and have done for so many years are very much appreciated.”


“We’ve got great assets,” he added. “There is no doubt about that. But our assets are great because of you and what you do.”


*From left: Energy Transfer co-CEOs Mackie McCrea and Tom Long.*


Jeff Darby, mayor of Nederland, read an official proclamation designating November 4 “Nederland Terminal Recognition Day” and recognizing the terminal’s impact on the local economy, the Nederland community and the growth of the U.S. energy industry.


*From left: Nederland Mayor Jeff Darby and Vice President of Nederland Operations Greg Mesthos.*


Inside the terminal offices, guests viewed historical artifacts and photos from the terminal’s operations over the past 125 years.


**History of the Nederland Terminal**


Following the 1901 Spindletop discovery about seven miles to the north, the Pew family developed dock space and crude oil storage along the Neches River. The following year, the Sun Oil Company tanker *SS Paraguay* carried Nederland’s first shipment, delivering 18,000 barrels of crude oil to the company’s newly built refinery in Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania.


During World War II, Sun Oil tankers transported critical crude oil and refined petroleum supplies up the coast to Marcus Hook and other refineries to fuel the U.S. and Allied war effort.


Over the ensuing decades, the Nederland Terminal continued to expand, playing a key role in the growth of the city of Nederland and the surrounding petroleum industry.


In 2002, the Nederland Terminal became part of Sunoco Logistics Partners (SXL), the master limited partnership Sunoco formed to own and operate its pipeline and terminal assets.


In 2017, SXL and Energy Transfer combined, bringing Nederland into the integrated Energy Transfer organization.


A major expansion in 2021 enabled the start of ethane exports at Nederland, bringing company-wide NGL export capacity to more than 1.1 million barrels per day (Bbls/d). This was followed in 2025 by the Nederland Flexport NGL Export Expansion Project, which added another 250,000 Bbls/d of NGL export capacity.


**The Nederland Terminal Today**


Today, the Nederland Terminal is unlike any facility of its kind. It is the largest, singularly owned above-ground crude oil storage facility in the U.S. and the largest NGL export facility in the world. It has approximately 33 million barrels of storage capacity and boasts unrivaled pipeline connectivity to almost every major production basin, as well as U.S. Department of Energy pipelines providing access to the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve.


For 125 years, the Nederland Terminal has evolved to meet the changing needs of America’s energy industry. Today, it stands as both a link to Energy Transfer’s history and a critical part of its future, connecting American energy to markets around the world.
